name: Muhammad Moosa Raza
affiliation: M.Sc. Ecology & Nature Management, RUDN University
tagline: Remote sensing for floods, drought and land change, built so the numbers can be checked

availability.detail: Open to positions in remote sensing, hydrology, land-system science and climate risk. Happy to discuss how this work could extend what your group is already doing.

about: I measure floods, drought and land change from satellites, mostly over Pakistan. Twelve studies so far, each one designed, built and published end to end: study areas chosen by measurement, models scored on years they never saw, and the code, training data and GIS exports released so the work can be taken apart by anyone who wants to.

The results I care most about are the ones that hold up under a second look. A flood susceptibility model that scores 0.962 on events it was never trained on. A national carbon account traceable to the pixel. A 44-year drought record that independently recovers the droughts and floods Pakistan actually had.

A PhD is where I want to take this further: building Earth observation measurements that are trustworthy enough to act on, and turning them into tools that people working on water and climate risk can use.

items.note: Tharparkar is rainless in 53.7% of pixel-months, which a standard gamma fit cannot represent. The zero-inflated fit gives a drought record that lines up with the documented 1999 to 2002 Sindh drought.

items.actualLabel: true peak, mapped scene by scene
items.note: Mapping every scene instead of one composite recovers the full inundation curve, and resolves two separate flood waves inside the 2022 monsoon.
Control years show the raw district signal is the ordinary double-cropping cycle. The flood impact survives as a map along the Indus belt, confirmed by an independent radar flood extent.
A predictor that was silently doing nothing, caught because a feature-importance plot looked wrong. Fixing it put the skill back into the flood susceptibility model.

details: Degree conferred with Honors-level performance. GPA 84.68 / 100 (ECTS Grade B)

Focus: Hydrology · GIS · Environmental systems · Water quality

bullets: Designed and published twelve end-to-end Earth observation studies over Pakistan, covering flood mapping, flood susceptibility, drought, soil moisture, crop mapping and speckle filtering
Built a flood susceptibility model for Layyah District that scores F1 = 0.962 and ROC-AUC = 0.996 on flood events held out of training, and mapped 547.8 km² of high-susceptibility land
Took the thesis work to national scale as a live Streamlit app accounting land cover and carbon for all 133 districts of Pakistan at 30 m
Reconstructed a 44-year drought record for Tharparkar that independently recovers the documented 1999 to 2002 Sindh drought and both major flood years
Held one methodological standard across every study: chronological validation, independent cross-sensor checks, and a stated uncertainty on every headline number
Released all of it as open code with training data, GIS exports and written limitations, so the results can be reproduced and argued with

experience.role: Master’s Thesis Researcher, Remote Sensing & Carbon Modelling
bullets: Built a multi-decadal (1993 to 2023) land-cover pipeline for Lahore District from the Landsat archive in Google Earth Engine, classifying four epochs with Random Forest
Quantified urban expansion of +117% and vegetation loss of 27,639 ha across the district over thirty years
Estimated ecosystem carbon dynamics at a loss of 534,110 Mg C between 1993 and 2023, on IPCC Tier 1 densities matched to the district's irrigated cropland, with a low to high band on every year
Extended the study into a CA-Markov projection to 2033 and 2043, combining Markov transition quantities, a Random Forest transition potential and cellular-automata allocation
Back-validated the projection to a Figure of Merit of 0.27 against 0.00 for a no-change null, on years that could be checked before anything was projected
Ran the InVEST carbon model as an independent check on the class-based estimate
Main contribution: showed how urban land transitions drive large-scale carbon loss in rapidly developing regions, and delivered a projection method that reports its own validation

Modelling & Analysis: Accuracy assessment (confusion matrix, Kappa, IoU, ROC)
